# Body lift parts and installation

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Select body lift height, source metric bolts and optional pucks while considering full kits or hose adjustments. [t1483]

[Partial] Pb blast body bolts three days before installing a body lift kit with a longer L-546 upper radiator hose. [t2081]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. [Partial] Select a body lift height of either one inch or two inches based on desired clearance.
2. [Partial] Source metric bolts, as standard hardware store sizes may not fit the frame rails perfectly.

_Procedure reported by [t1483]._

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t2081] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Pb blast the body bolts three days before installation for easier removal.
2. [Partial] Remove the lower fan shroud.

</details>

## Tools

- Impact wrench [t2081]
- Sockets [t2081]

## Parts

- [Partial] 1-inch Lift Bolts: Metric size preferred [t1483]
- Body lift kit, bolts and pucks: Can be pieced together from various sources or bought as a kit. [t2081]
- Longer upper radiator hose (L-546) [t2081]
- [Partial] Zone Off-road Pucks, optional: $3 per piece, available with free shipping on eBay or individually at local stores. [t1483]

## Tips & gotchas

- [Partial] Consider buying a full kit from a vendor like Allan Fasteners if hunting for individual parts becomes tedious. [t1483]
- [Partial] Look for longer upper radiator hoses to compensate for the frame moving upward; trim them down if necessary. [t1483]
- Buy the longer version of an upper radiator hose to ensure proper fitment. [t2081]
- If buying a pre-made kit, verify if it includes a radiator relocation piece or requires a separate longer hose. [t2081]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Using a stock short upper radiator hose that snaps off the plastic fitting when lifting begins. [t2081]
